title: Update AGENTS.md to enforce small-step workflow
description: Update the AGENTS.md file at the project root to add a mandatory 'Small-Step Workflow' section. It must state that agents MUST only do one small step at a time, verify it works (tests pass, no errors), and ONLY THEN move to the next step. This is essential and must never be forgotten. Add it near the top, right after Quickstart or in a dedicated 'Workflow Rules' section. Also add a Gotcha about it.

If the top-level brave API setting has been configured, the per-bot Brave Search API key should default to that value.

title: Debug embedding dimensions mismatch in puck memory save
description: Puck agent fails to save memory because the database expects 768-dimension vectors (nomic-embed-text) but the fallback embedding model (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) produces 384-dimension vectors. Also there is a logging error where config.py tries to log an empty embedding_model with None dimension. Investigate the full chain from config resolution to DB schema.

title: Investigate config.py embedding model resolution and logging error
description: Read src/pillywiggins/config.py. The docker logs show: (1) 'No Ollama embedding model found; falling back to HuggingFace all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (384-dim)' and (2) 'Explicit embedding model '%s' with dimension %d' logged with ('', None) causing TypeError. Trace how resolve_embedding_config() works. Why is the embedding_model empty string? Why does it fall back to HuggingFace when Ollama is available? Document findings.

title: Investigate DB vector dimension configuration
description: Read the SQL schema or migration files that create the private_memory/council_memory tables with vector columns. Determine how the vector dimension is set and whether it is hardcoded to 768 for nomic-embed-text. Also check src/pillywiggins/memory/private.py and src/pillywiggins/memory/council.py for any dimension-related setup. Document the mismatch between DB schema and runtime embedding dimension.

title: Investigate embeddings.py provider initialization
description: Read src/pillywiggins/memory/embeddings.py. Trace how the embedding provider is initialized at runtime. Does it read the resolved config? How does it select between Ollama and HuggingFace? Why does it produce 384-dim vectors when the DB expects 768? Document the initialization chain and any missing config propagation.

title: Fix embedding model env poisoning on fallback
description: When resolve_embedding_config() falls back to HuggingFace, it sets os.environ['EMBEDDING_MODEL'] = ''. Any subsequent Settings() instance reads this empty string, enters the 'explicit model' branch, and crashes with TypeError at line 89 (logging '%d' with None). Fix: don't pollute os.environ with empty string; use a sentinel value or avoid setting it at all.

title: Stop embedding model env poisoning and fix TypeError
description: In src/pillywiggins/config.py resolve_embedding_config(), when falling back to HuggingFace (embedding_model becomes empty string), stop writing os.environ['EMBEDDING_MODEL'] = ''. This poisons every subsequent Settings() instance. Instead, only write to os.environ when the value is meaningful. Also guard the '%d' format in the explicit-model log so it handles unknown models gracefully (e.g., log a warning instead of crashing). Add a test for the fallback path. Verify by running pytest.

title: Add startup DB migration for embedding dimension mismatch
description: When the runtime embedding model produces a different dimension than the existing DB schema (e.g., fallback from nomic-embed-text/768d to all-MiniLM-L6-v2/384d), memory save fails with asyncpg DataError. Strategy A: add a startup-time ALTER TABLE in PrivateMemory.connect() and CouncilMemory.connect() that checks the current column dimension and ALTERs it to match the resolved setting.embedding_dimension.

title: Add ALTER TABLE migration to PrivateMemory.connect()
description: In PrivateMemory.connect(), after creating the pool and registering vector, add a check: query information_schema or pg_attribute for the private_memory.embedding column dimension. If it does not match self._embedding_dimension, run ALTER TABLE private_memory ALTER COLUMN embedding TYPE vector(NEW_DIM). This handles model changes dynamically. Add tests that verify the migration path with a mocked connection or real test DB. Do NOT change config.py or embeddings.py.

title: Add ALTER TABLE migration to CouncilMemory.connect()
description: In CouncilMemory.connect(), after creating the pool and registering vector, add a check: query information_schema or pg_attribute for the council_memory.embedding column dimension. If it does not match self._embedding_dimension, run ALTER TABLE council_memory ALTER COLUMN embedding TYPE vector(NEW_DIM). Handles runtime model dimension changes. Add tests. Do NOT change config.py or embeddings.py.

title: Fix embedding model 'auto' leaking from .env to embed() calls
description: Puck logs show: 'model "auto" not found, try pulling it first' with 404 from Ollama. The .env file has EMBEDDING_MODEL=auto. resolve_embedding_config() at startup falls back to HF and sets embedding_model='' locally, but some embed() call site creates a fresh Settings() which re-reads 'auto' from .env and passes it to embed(..., model='auto'). Need to trace the call chain and fix the leak.

title: Trace embed() call chain for model='auto' leak
description: Trace the call chain from the agent processing a message to the embed() call that passes model='auto'. Check base.py, brain.py, or any tool that creates a Settings() instance and calls embed(). Determine why the resolved config (empty string / HF fallback) is not being propagated. Document findings. Do NOT fix yet.

title: Stop brain.py tool functions from creating fresh Settings() instances
description: brain.py tool functions (query_council_memory, share_to_council, recall_private_memory, save_to_private_memory) create fresh Settings() instances inside tool calls. Since .env has EMBEDDING_MODEL=auto, each fresh Settings() re-reads 'auto' and passes it to embed(..., model='auto'), causing Ollama 404 'model auto not found'. The fix is to stop creating fresh Settings() in tools — instead pass resolved settings through AgentDeps or use the module-level settings object that was resolved at startup.

title: Pass resolved embedding config through AgentDeps to brain tools
description: In src/pillywiggins/agents/brain.py, the four tool functions create fresh Settings() instances. Since the .env still has EMBEDDING_MODEL=auto, each fresh Settings() re-reads it and passes 'auto' to embed(). The fix: pass resolved embedding config (model, base_url, api_key, provider, dimension) through AgentDeps so tools don't need to create Settings(). Add embedding_model, llm_base_url, llm_api_key, llm_provider, embedding_dimension to AgentDeps. Update all four tool functions to use deps.embedding_model etc. instead of Settings(). Update tests. Verify by running pytest.

title: Re-add safe EMBEDDING_MODEL env write for HF fallback
description: Our previous fix removed os.environ['EMBEDDING_MODEL'] = '' from the fallback path to prevent TypeError crashes. But brain.py tool functions create fresh Settings() instances that re-read 'auto' from .env, passing model='auto' to embed() which causes Ollama 404. The embed() function requires model='' to trigger HF fallback. We need to re-add os.environ['EMBEDDING_MODEL'] = '' but now it's safe because we added the log guard for None dimensions.

title: Re-add safe os.environ['EMBEDDING_MODEL'] = '' to fallback path
description: In src/pillywiggins/config.py resolve_embedding_config() fallback path (the else block at ~line 116), re-add os.environ['EMBEDDING_MODEL'] = ''. The log guard we added earlier (if dim is not None before %d format) makes this safe. Update the test test_settings_resolve_embedding_fallback_no_env_poisoning in tests/test_config.py: rename it to reflect that env IS written (safely), and assert that a subsequent Settings() instance reads the empty string without crashing. Verify by running pytest.

title: Gracefully handle Telegram TimedOut in telegram adapter
description: Puck occasionally hits telegram.error.TimedOut when sending replies back to Telegram. This is a transient network issue that python-telegram-bot already retries internally, but currently logs a full noisy traceback. Add a try/except around the send call in _on_message to catch TimedOut and log a concise warning instead of the full exception traceback.

title: Catch TimedOut in _on_message and log concise warning
description: In src/pillywiggins/adapters/telegram_adapter.py, find the _on_message method and the send() call. Wrap the send call in a try/except that catches telegram.error.TimedOut. On timeout, log a concise warning like 'Timed out sending reply to Telegram chat {chat_id}; message may be retried automatically' instead of letting the full traceback propagate. Do NOT suppress other exceptions — only catch TimedOut. Add a test for this path. Verify by running pytest.

title: Add system prompt rule: trust retrieved memory over conversation history
description: When an agent retrieves a memory that contradicts something in the conversation history/context window, the LLM gets confused and presents both as valid. The fix is to add a simple rule to the system prompt that tells the agent to always prioritize retrieved memory over conversation history when they conflict.

title: Investigate prompt construction and add memory-priority rule
description: Read src/pillywiggins/agents/brain.py to understand how the system prompt is constructed for PydanticAI, and read one or two personality YAML files (e.g., personalities/puck.yaml) to see if there's an existing memory-related instruction. Determine the best place to inject the rule: either in the personality YAML files (applies per-personality) or programmatically in brain.py (applies to all agents). Add the rule: 'When retrieved memories contradict information in the conversation history, always trust the memory as the more up-to-date and authoritative source.' Verify by running pytest. Do NOT change memory storage or retrieval logic.
